category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: To identify the lymph node nearest to a primary tumour in melanoma or breast cancer, a radiolabelled colloid is injected to perform a [___].
back:
• Sentinel node biopsy
• Uses a gamma camera to pinpoint the first draining node
• Essential for histological diagnosis and staging

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A patient with inoperable caecal cancer presents with symptoms of bowel obstruction. A surgical ileo-transverse anastomosis is performed. Identify the primary goal of this intervention.
back:
• Surgical palliation
• Alleviates symptoms of bowel obstruction
• Improves quality of life without curative intent

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Explain the role and extent of radical surgery in the management of solid tumours.
back:
• Removal of primary tumour with wide margins
• Excision of regional lymph node drainage
• Aims for local control and prevention of lymphatic spread

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Contrast the impact of a new, highly sensitive staging investigation on stage-specific prognosis versus the overall population survival (Will Rogers phenomenon).
back:
• Stage-specific: Artefactual improvement in prognosis for all stages
• Overall: No change in prognosis for the pooled group
• Cause: Movement of patients with occult metastases to higher stages

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Identify the clinical scenario where resection or ablation (cryotherapy/RFA) of liver metastases can lead to long-term survival in one-third of patients.
back:
• Metastases arising from colorectal cancer
• Isolated or resectable liver involvement
• Successful removal of all detectable disease

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: The international system used to map the extent of cancer based on primary tumour size, regional node involvement, and distant spread is the [___].
back:
• TNM staging system
• Governed by UICC and AJCC
• Determines if treatment should be locoregional or systemic

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A patient with suspected gastric cancer undergoes laparoscopy before definitive resection. Explain the specific diagnostic utility of this step over cross-sectional imaging.
back:
• Identifies widespread peritoneal disease
• Detects small liver metastases missed on CT/MRI
• Provides tissue for histological diagnosis in malignant ascites

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Describe the functional difference between the 'multidisciplinary' and 'multiprofessional' components of an oncology team.
back:
• Multidisciplinary: Various medically qualified specialists (surgeons, pathologists)
• Multiprofessional: Specialists from non-medical backgrounds (nurses, social workers)
• Ensures comprehensive, transparent patient management

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Contrast the surgical approach for curative intent versus palliative intent in a patient with a symptomatic primary tumour and distant metastases.
back:
• Curative: Radical removal of primary and nodes (not applicable here)
• Palliative: Removal or bypass of primary to improve quality of life
• Outcome: Palliation focuses on symptom control, not survival

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Name the palliative bypass procedure used to relieve jaundice in a patient with unresectable carcinoma of the head of the pancreas.
back:
• Cholecysto-jejunostomy or Choledocho-jejunostomy
• Alleviates biliary obstruction
• Focuses on symptom relief when cure is impossible

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: The surgical technique used to identify the first draining lymph node in breast cancer or melanoma by injecting a radiolabelled colloid is [___].
back:
● Sentinel node biopsy
● Involves gamma camera scanning
● Pinpoints node nearest to tumour for histological diagnosis
● Minimizes unnecessary radical lymphadenectomy

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A 65-year-old male with metastatic, inoperable caecal cancer presents with worsening abdominal distension and vomiting. The indicated palliative surgical procedure is [___].
back:
● Ileo-transverse anastomosis
● Aimed at bypassing the obstruction
● Focuses on symptom relief/quality of life
● Does not alter the ultimate oncological outcome

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Explain the role of 'in situ' ablation (cryotherapy or radiofrequency energy) in the management of colorectal cancer.
back:
● Used for multiple liver metastases
● Alternative when surgical resection is not feasible
● Destroys tumour tissue while sparing normal parenchyma
● Can lead to long-term survival in selected patients

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Contrast the surgical approach for localized colorectal primary tumour versus isolated renal cell carcinoma pulmonary metastases.
back:
● Primary: Radical resection of tumour plus surrounding tissue and lymphatic drainage.
● Metastatic: Targeted pulmonary resection (metastasectomy) if disease is isolated.
● Primary focuses on local control; Metastatic focuses on extending survival in oligometastatic disease.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: What are the core components of the multidisciplinary team (MDT) in surgical oncology?
back:
● Site-specialist/Surgical Oncologist
● Radiologists and Pathologists
● Medical and Clinical (Radiation) Oncologists
● Palliative care physicians and Nurse specialists

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: In the TNM staging system, the designation 'T3' for colorectal cancer specifically indicates that the tumour has invaded [___].
back:
● Through the muscularis propria
● Into the subserosa or retroperitoneal tissues
● Subdivided by depth of invasion (a-d)
● Critical for determining adjuvant therapy needs

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A patient with malignant ascites requires a definitive tissue diagnosis. Which surgical intervention is most appropriate for staging and sampling?
back:
● Diagnostic Laparoscopy
● Allows direct visualization of peritoneal surfaces
● Detects small liver metastases missed on CT
● Facilitates targeted biopsy of nodules or fluid

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Describe the 'Will Rogers Phenomenon' (Stage Shift) resulting from advances in imaging technology.
back:
● Advanced imaging detects occult metastases earlier
● Patients migrate from 'localized' to 'metastatic' stages
● Artificially improves survival rates for both stages
● Overall survival for the entire group remains unchanged

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Contrast the definitions of 'multidisciplinary' versus 'multiprofessional' teams in an oncology context.
back:
● Multidisciplinary: Includes various medically qualified specialists (e.g., surgeons, pathologists).
● Multiprofessional: Includes specialists from non-medical backgrounds (e.g., social workers, physiotherapists).
● Both aim to ensure comprehensive, appropriate patient management.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Which malignancy historically required a staging laparotomy that is now largely redundant due to improved imaging and chemotherapy?
back:
● Lymphoma (specifically Hodgkin lymphoma)
● Replaced by modern cross-sectional imaging (PET/CT)
● Surgery now limited to primary biopsy for diagnosis
● Shift reflects priority of systemic treatment over surgery

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: The phenomenon where improved staging technology paradoxically increases survival rates in every individual stage while leaving the overall group prognosis unchanged is known as [___].
back:
- Stage shift (or Will Rogers phenomenon).
- Occurs due to detection of occult metastases by better imaging.
- Enriches each stage with patients having better-than-average prognoses.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A 65-year-old male with unresectable carcinoma of the head of the pancreas presents with severe obstructive jaundice. The most appropriate surgical palliative procedure to alleviate his jaundice is [___].
back:
- Cholecysto-jejunostomy or Choledocho-jejunostomy.
- This is a biliary bypass procedure.
- Goal is symptom relief and improved quality of life without curative intent.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Explain the role of Sentinel Node Biopsy in the diagnostic management of melanoma or breast cancer.
back:
- Involves injecting radiolabelled colloid or dye around the primary tumour.
- Identifies the first (sentinel) draining lymph node via gamma camera.
- Histological assessment determines if radical lymphadenectomy is necessary.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Contrast the composition of a 'multidisciplinary' team with a 'multiprofessional' team in the context of oncological management.
back:
- Multidisciplinary: Consists of various medically qualified specialists (surgeons, pathologists, radiologists).
- Multiprofessional: Includes specialists from non-medical backgrounds (nurses, social workers, physiotherapists).
- Both aim for holistic, transparent clinical decision-making.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: List the three anatomical components that must be removed during radical surgery for a solid tumor to ensure local control.
back:
- The primary tumour.
- Surrounding healthy tissue (safety margin).
- Regional lymph node drainage pathways.
- Goal is preventing both local recurrence and lymphatic spread.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: In patients presenting with malignant ascites where imaging is inconclusive, [___] is the surgical procedure of choice for obtaining tissue diagnosis and staging.
back:
- Laparoscopy.
- Useful for detecting widespread peritoneal disease.
- Identifies small liver metastases missed by cross-sectional imaging (CT/MRI).

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A patient with colorectal cancer has localized liver metastases. State the potential for long-term survival with resection and the alternative 'in situ' surgical options.
back:
- Long-term survival is achieved in approximately one-third of patients post-resection.
- Alternatives include cryotherapy or radiofrequency ablation (RFA).
- These methods use thermal energy for localized destruction.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Describe the physiological principle of 'selective toxicity' and its role in the non-surgical treatment of cancer.
back:
- Treatment is designed to be selectively toxic to tumour cells.
- Goal is to spare normal tissues from severe or permanent damage.
- Underpins the calculation of optimal doses and delivery schedules.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Differentiate between the primary goals of curative surgery versus palliative surgical interventions in cancer patients.
back:
- Curative: Removal of all detectable disease for long-term survival (e.g., radical mastectomy).
- Palliative: Symptom relief and quality of life enhancement (e.g., ileo-transverse anastomosis for obstruction).
- Palliation does not typically alter the ultimate outcome/mortality.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Identify the two most commonly used clinicopathological staging systems for colorectal cancer.
back:
- TNM (Tumour, Nodes, Metastases) system by UICC/AJCC.
- Dukes staging (or Modified Astler-Coller).
- These systems guide the choice between local surgery and systemic therapy.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: The phenomenon where improved staging technology detects occult metastases, seemingly improving prognosis in specific stages while overall survival remains unchanged, is the [___].
back:
● Will Rogers phenomenon (Stage Shift).
● Results from reclassifying patients into more advanced stages.
● Prognosis for the entire group remains constant.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A 70-year-old male with unresectable carcinoma of the head of the pancreas presents with severe obstructive jaundice. The most appropriate surgical palliative procedure to bypass this biliary obstruction is [___].
back:
● Cholecysto-jejunostomy or choledocho-jejunostomy.
● Relieves jaundice symptoms.
● Improves quality of life without intent to cure the underlying cancer.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Explain the role of sentinel node biopsy in the staging of breast cancer or melanoma.
back:
● Injection of radiolabelled colloid near the tumour.
● Gamma camera pinpointing the nearest (sentinel) node.
● Targeted removal for histological diagnosis to avoid radical lymphadenectomy.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Contrast the composition and purpose of a 'multidisciplinary' team versus a 'multiprofessional' team in oncology management.
back:
● Multidisciplinary: Various medically qualified specialists (surgeons, pathologists, radiologists).
● Multiprofessional: Includes non-medical specialists (nurses, social workers, physiotherapists).
● Ensures comprehensive, transparent, and expert management decisions.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Outline the primary technical objectives when performing radical surgery for a solid primary tumour.
back:
● Complete removal of the primary tumour.
● Excision of surrounding tissue and associated lymph node drainage.
● Meticulous handling to avoid tumour disruption and local seeding.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: In patients with malignant ascites where imaging is inconclusive, the surgical procedure used to obtain tissue for diagnosis and detect occult peritoneal disease is [___].
back:
● Laparoscopy.
● Identifies small liver metastases or peritoneal spread missed by CT/MRI.
● Essential for accurate intra-abdominal staging.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A patient with colorectal cancer is found to have three isolated liver metastases. Justify the surgical rationale for performing a liver resection in this metastatic case.
back:
● Potentially curative despite metastatic spread.
● Successful resection leads to long-term survival in approximately one-third of patients.
● Can be combined with in situ ablation (cryotherapy).

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Explain why meticulous dissection and 'not disrupting the primary tumour' are vital surgical principles during cancer excision.
back:
● Prevents local recurrence by avoiding cell spillage.
● Ensures definitive local control of the disease.
● Directly impacts the possibility of achieving a cure in localised tumours.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Differentiate the surgical intent of an ileo-transverse anastomosis from a radical hemicolectomy in a patient with caecal cancer.
back:
● Ileo-transverse anastomosis: Palliative bypass to alleviate bowel obstruction in inoperable cases.
● Radical hemicolectomy: Curative removal of the primary tumour and lymphatic drainage.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Define the specific components of the UICC/AJCC TNM staging system used to classify the extent of cancer.
back:
● T: Size or local extent of the primary tumour.
● N: Involvement of regional lymph nodes.
● M: Presence or absence of distant metastases.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: The surgical technique of [___] involves injecting radiolabelled colloid to identify and biopsy the nearest lymph node to a primary tumor in melanoma or breast cancer.
back:
● Sentinel node biopsy
● Identifies first node in drainage basin
● Minimizes need for extensive lymphadenectomy

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A 65-year-old patient with inoperable caecal cancer presents with worsening abdominal distension and vomiting. The most appropriate surgical intervention to manage these symptoms is [___].
back:
● Ileo-transverse anastomosis
● Surgical bypass procedure
● Goal: Palliative relief of bowel obstruction

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Explain the biological objective behind performing 'Radical Surgery' for solid tumors.
back:
● Local control of primary tumor
● Excision of surrounding tissue margins
● Removal of regional lymph node drainage to prevent spread

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Contrast the clinical utility of radical surgery versus ultra-radical surgery in the management of breast cancer.
back:
● Radical surgery: Essential for obtaining local control.
● Ultra-radical surgery: No proven benefit in preventing metastatic disease over simple mastectomy.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Define the 'Will Rogers Phenomenon' (stage shift) in modern oncology staging.
back:
● Artefactual improvement in stage-specific prognosis
● Caused by advanced imaging detecting occult metastases
● Overall group survival remains unchanged

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: In patients presenting with malignant ascites of unknown origin, [___] is the primary surgical procedure used for obtaining tissue and staging.
back:
● Laparoscopy
● Allows direct visualization of peritoneal disease
● Used to detect small liver metastases missed by imaging

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A patient with solitary liver metastasis from colorectal cancer is considered for surgery. What is the expected long-term survival rate following successful resection?
back:
● Approximately one-third (33%) of patients
● Surgery provides a realistic hope for cure in metastatic disease

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: How do 'multidisciplinary' teams differ from 'multiprofessional' teams in a clinical oncology setting?
back:
● Multidisciplinary: Medically qualified specialists (Pathologists, Radiologists).
● Multiprofessional: Inclusion of non-medical specialists (Nurses, Social workers).

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Contrast the intent of a cholecysto-jejunostomy with that of a radical resection in pancreatic cancer.
back:
● Cholecysto-jejunostomy: Palliative (alleviates jaundice/improves quality of life).
● Radical Resection: Curative (removes primary disease for survival).

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Identify two surgical energy modalities used for the 'in situ' ablation of multiple liver metastases.
back:
● Cryotherapy
● Radiofrequency energy (RFA)
● Used when resection is not feasible

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: The paradox where improved diagnostic technology detects occult metastases, causing an apparent increase in survival for individual stages without changing overall group prognosis, is known as the [___].
back:
- Will Rogers phenomenon (Stage shift).
- Occurs when patients with better prognoses enrich each stage.
- Overall prognosis for the pooled group remains unchanged.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A 55-year-old male with unresectable carcinoma of the head of the pancreas presents with obstructive jaundice. Identify the surgical procedure indicated to alleviate his symptoms.
back:
- Surgical bypass procedures.
- Examples: Cholecysto-jejunostomy or choledocho-jejunostomy.
- Purpose: Palliative relief of jaundice (not curative).

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Explain the role of sentinel node biopsy in the staging mechanism of breast cancer or melanoma.
back:
- Radiolabelled colloid/dye is injected around the primary tumor.
- Gamma camera or visual tracking identifies the first draining (sentinel) node.
- Node is removed for histological assessment of metastatic spread.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A patient with gastric cancer has no metastases on CT scan, yet the surgeon recommends a laparoscopy. Contrast the diagnostic utility of staging laparoscopy versus cross-sectional imaging in this case.
back:
- Laparoscopy: Detects small peritoneal seedlings and liver surface metastases.
- Imaging (CT/MRI): Often misses occult peritoneal or small intrahepatic disease.
- Clinical utility: Prevents unnecessary radical surgery in widespread disease.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Identify the primary surgical intervention for a patient with isolated liver metastases secondary to colorectal cancer that offers a chance for long-term survival.
back:
- Successful surgical resection of all detectable disease.
- Alternative: In situ ablation (cryotherapy or radiofrequency energy).
- Result: Long-term survival in approximately one-third of patients.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: In the UICC/AJCC staging system for colorectal cancer, the parameter 'T3' refers to a tumor that invades through the [___].
back:
- Muscularis propria into subserosa or retroperitoneal tissues.
- Categorized further by depth of invasion (a-d).
- Essential for determining local stage and treatment.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A 65-year-old female is diagnosed with a symptomatic primary tumor but has widespread distant metastases. Explain the rationale for performing surgery on the primary site in this scenario.
back:
- Palliative surgery.
- Goal: Increase quality of life by removing symptoms.
- Outcome: Does not change the ultimate oncological survival (outcome).

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Contrast radical surgery with ultra-radical surgery regarding their impact on preventing metastatic disease in breast cancer.
back:
- Radical surgery: Essential for local control and preventing recurrence.
- Ultra-radical surgery: Randomized trials show no significant effect on preventing metastatic disease.
- Emphasis: Meticulous technique is more critical than extreme tissue margins.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Distinguish between 'multidisciplinary' and 'multiprofessional' teams within the context of a modern oncology unit.
back:
- Multidisciplinary: Various medically qualified specialists (surgeons, oncologists, pathologists).
- Multiprofessional: Inclusion of non-medical specialists (nurses, social workers, physiotherapists).
- Goal: Holistic and appropriate patient management.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Name the specific clinical scenario where pulmonary resection is commonly performed for isolated lung metastases with potential survival benefit.
back:
- Isolated lung metastases from renal cell carcinoma.
- Purpose: Removal of localized secondary disease after primary control.
- One of the few indications for metastatic pulmonary surgery.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
coreConcept: Will Rogers Phenomenon in Cancer Staging
front: The phenomenon where improved diagnostic technology identifies occult metastases, leading to an apparent but artefactual improvement in stage-specific prognosis while overall survival remains unchanged, is known as [___].
back:
- Stage shift
- Also called the Will Rogers phenomenon
- Results from enriched prognosis in each stage group
- Overall group prognosis remains static.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A 55-year-old female with a breast lump undergoes an injection of radiolabelled colloid to identify the first draining lymph node for histological assessment. Identify this procedure and its primary clinical goal.
back:
- Sentinel node biopsy
- Identifies the node nearest to the tumor
- Minimizes surgical morbidity
- Ensures accurate pathological staging.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Explain the role of laparoscopy in the staging of intra-abdominal malignancies like gastric or oesophageal cancer compared to traditional imaging.
back:
- Detects small peritoneal deposits missed by CT/MRI
- Identifies occult surface liver metastases
- Allows direct tissue biopsy for diagnosis
- Utilizes laparoscopic ultrasound for intrahepatic lesions.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Contrast the therapeutic outcomes of radical surgery versus ultra-radical surgery based on randomized clinical trials for solid tumors like breast cancer.
back:
- Radical surgery: Removes primary + margins + lymphatics for local control
- Ultra-radical surgery: Extensive tissue removal
- Evidence: Ultra-radical techniques rarely improve survival or prevent distant metastasis over radical surgery.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: List three distinct surgical roles in cancer management that do not involve the removal of the primary tumor site.
back:
- Diagnosis (e.g., lymph node biopsy)
- Reconstruction (e.g., plastic surgery post-excision)
- Palliation (e.g., bypassing an obstruction).

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: In the TNM staging system for colorectal cancer, the T-category (T1 to T4) is specifically determined by [___] rather than tumor diameter.
back:
- Depth of invasion into the bowel wall layers
- T1: Submucosa; T2: Muscularis propria; T3: Subserosa/retroperitoneal tissues
- T4: Perforation or direct organ invasion.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A patient with inoperable pancreatic head cancer presents with severe obstructive jaundice. Suggest the most appropriate palliative surgical intervention to improve quality of life.
back:
- Biliary bypass procedure
- Options: Cholecysto-jejunostomy or choledocho-jejunostomy
- Aim: Alleviate jaundice and pruritus
- Does not alter the ultimate oncological outcome.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Describe the mechanism by which surgical resection of metastatic disease can be curative, specifically in colorectal cancer patients.
back:
- Applicable to isolated liver metastases
- Successful resection of all detectable disease
- Leads to long-term survival in ~33% of cases
- Alternative: In situ ablation (Cryotherapy/RFA).

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Differentiate between the dose-response characteristics of surgery versus non-surgical treatments like radiotherapy.
back:
- Surgery: Difficult to quantify in discrete units
- Radiotherapy/Drugs: Sigmoidal dose-response curves
- Goal: Selective toxicity (maximal uncomplicated cure)
- Narrow range between therapeutic success and tissue disaster.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: State the primary advantage of a Multidisciplinary Team (MDT) approach in oncological decision-making.
back:
- Open, transparent, and explicit decision-making
- Simultaneous opinions from multiple specialties
- Ensures patient receives the most appropriate, evidence-based care
- Facilitates cross-specialty education.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: The phenomenon where improved staging technology falsely appears to improve prognosis in all individual stages without changing overall survival is known as [___].
back:
Will Rogers phenomenon (Stage Shift).
- Patients are reassigned to more accurate stages due to better imaging.
- Prognosis of each stage appears enriched.
- Total population outcome remains unchanged.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A patient with inoperable caecal cancer presents with symptoms of intestinal obstruction. The surgical bypass procedure indicated for palliation is [___].
back:
Ileo-transverse anastomosis.
- Bypasses the obstructive primary tumor.
- Restores bowel continuity to alleviate symptoms.
- Improves quality of life without intending to cure the malignancy.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Explain the role of radiolabelled colloids and gamma cameras in the surgical staging of breast cancer.
back:
Mechanism of Sentinel Node Biopsy:
- Colloid is injected around the primary tumor.
- Gamma camera identifies the nearest (sentinel) lymph node.
- Node removal and histology determine if lymphatic spread has occurred.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Contrast the clinical goals and outcomes of radical surgery versus ultra-radical surgery in the management of solid tumors like breast cancer.
back:
Radical vs Ultra-radical Surgery:
- Radical: Removes primary tumor and regional lymphatics for local control.
- Ultra-radical: Previously thought to prevent metastasis; trials show no survival benefit over standard radical procedures.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Identify the specific clinical scenario where surgical resection of liver metastases is considered a potentially curative intervention.
back:
Colorectal Cancer Metastases:
- Resection of all detectable liver disease is appropriate.
- Can lead to long-term survival in one-third of patients.
- In situ ablation (cryotherapy/radiofrequency) is an alternative.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: In the TNM staging system developed by the UICC, the 'N' component specifically assesses [___].
back:
Regional Lymph Nodes:
- Evaluates the presence and extent of node involvement.
- Crucial for determining if locoregional or systemic therapy is required.
- NX indicates nodes cannot be assessed.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A patient with unresectable carcinoma of the pancreatic head presents with obstructive jaundice. Which surgical intervention provides the most effective palliation?
back:
Biliary Bypass (Cholecysto- or Choledocho-jejunostomy):
- Diverts bile flow away from the tumor obstruction.
- Effectively alleviates jaundice.
- Focuses on symptom control and patient comfort.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Describe how laparoscopy provides a diagnostic advantage over cross-sectional imaging in staging intra-abdominal malignancies like gastric cancer.
back:
Laparoscopic Staging Advantages:
- Identifies widespread peritoneal disease missed by CT/MRI.
- Detects small surface liver metastases.
- Allows for direct visualization and tissue biopsy for histological confirmation.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Distinguish between the terms 'multidisciplinary' and 'multiprofessional' within a cancer management team.
back:
MDT Composition:
- Multidisciplinary: Medically qualified specialists (surgeons, pathologists, radiologists).
- Multiprofessional: Non-medical specialists (specialist nurses, social workers, physiotherapists).
- Both ensure holistic, evidence-based patient management.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: List the primary roles of surgery in oncology apart from the removal of the primary disease.
back:
Surgical Roles:
- Diagnosis (e.g., lymph node biopsy).
- Staging (e.g., laparoscopy).
- Removal of metastatic disease.
- Palliation (bypass).
- Prevention and Reconstruction.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: The phenomenon where improved imaging techniques detect occult metastases, causing an apparent improvement in stage-specific prognosis without changing overall survival, is known as [___].
back:
Will Rogers Phenomenon (Stage Shift).
- Results from better detection technology.
- Artefactual improvement in individual stage prognosis.
- Overall group prognosis remains unchanged.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A 65-year-old patient with inoperable caecal cancer presents with vomiting and abdominal distension. An ileo-transverse anastomosis is performed to bypass the tumor. This surgical role is termed [___].
back:
Surgical Palliation.
- Alleviates symptoms like obstruction or jaundice.
- Improves quality of life.
- Does not intend to cure the primary disease.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Explain the biological rationale behind radical surgery involving the removal of the primary tumor and its surrounding lymph node drainage.
back:
Local Control and Prevention:
- Ensures complete local disease clearance.
- Prevents tumor spread through lymphatics.
- Reduces risk of local recurrence.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Contrast the composition of an oncology 'multidisciplinary' team with that of a 'multiprofessional' team.
back:
Composition Difference:
- Multidisciplinary: Various medically qualified specialists (Pathologists, Radiologists, Surgeons).
- Multiprofessional: Includes non-medical specialists (Nurses, Social workers, Physiotherapists).

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Identify the primary clinical indication and potential outcome of surgical resection for liver metastases in colorectal cancer patients.
back:
Resection Indication:
- All detectable disease must be resectable.
- Can lead to long-term survival in ~33% of patients.
- Used when metastases are isolated.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: In the staging of intra-abdominal malignancies like gastric cancer, [___] is the preferred surgical adjunct to detect small liver metastases or peritoneal disease missed by CT scans.
back:
Laparoscopy (with/without Ultrasound).
- Diagnoses occult peritoneal disease.
- Detects small intrahepatic metastases.
- Prevents unnecessary radical surgery.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A patient suspected of having lymphoma requires a definitive diagnosis. Name the specific surgical procedure typically required to provide adequate tissue for histological analysis.
back:
Lymph node biopsy.
- Provides architecture for histological diagnosis.
- Necessary when non-invasive imaging is insufficient.
- Key for lymphoma subtyping.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: How does the principle of 'selective toxicity' guide the non-surgical management of tumors compared to surgical excision?
back:
Treatment Balance:
- Targets tumor cells while sparing normal tissue.
- Determines optimal dose for 'uncomplicated cure'.
- Uses sigmoidal dose-response curves to define safety margins.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Distinguish between Dukes Stage B and Dukes Stage C in the clinicopathological staging of colorectal cancer.
back:
Nodal Involvement:
- Dukes B: Invasion through muscularis propria (T3/T4) with NO lymph node involvement (N0).
- Dukes C: Any T stage with regional lymph node metastases (N1/N2).

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: List the six primary roles of surgery in the comprehensive management of cancer.
back:
Surgical Roles:
- Diagnosis
- Removal of primary disease
- Removal of metastatic disease
- Palliation
- Prevention
- Reconstruction

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: In the management of intra-abdominal malignancies like gastric cancer, [___] is a vital surgical tool for identifying occult peritoneal disease or small liver metastases missed by imaging.
back:
• Laparoscopy
• Often used with laparoscopic ultrasound
• Essential for accurate staging before planning radical resection

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A 60-year-old male with inoperable caecal cancer presents with symptoms of bowel obstruction. The most appropriate surgical palliative procedure to alleviate his symptoms is [___].
back:
• Ileo-transverse anastomosis
• Bypasses the site of obstruction
• Aimed at improving quality of life without curative intent

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Explain the biological role and procedure of sentinel lymph node biopsy in the context of melanoma or breast cancer.
back:
• Identifies the first node receiving drainage from the tumor
• Involves injecting radiolabelled colloid or dye
• Prevents unnecessary radical lymph node dissection if the node is negative

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Contrast the surgical goals of 'radical' resection versus 'palliative' surgical intervention in oncological management.
back:
• Radical: Removal of primary tumor, surrounding tissue, and lymph drainage for cure.
• Palliative: Bypass or debulking to relieve symptoms (e.g., jaundice) without curative intent.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Identify the clinical scenarios where surgical resection of metastatic disease is high-yield and potentially curative.
back:
• Liver metastases from colorectal cancer
• Isolated lung metastases from renal cell carcinoma
• Can involve resection or in-situ ablation (radiofrequency/cryotherapy)

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: The phenomenon where improved imaging technology detects occult metastases, causing an artefactual improvement in stage-specific prognosis while overall survival is unchanged, is [___].
back:
• Stage shift
• Also known as the Will Rogers phenomenon
• Results from enriching stages with patients having better baseline prognoses

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A patient with unresectable carcinoma of the head of the pancreas presents with severe obstructive jaundice. Name the primary surgical bypass options.
back:
• Cholecysto-jejunostomy
• Choledocho-jejunostomy
• Relieves biliary obstruction to improve quality of life and comfort

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Explain why meticulous technique and avoiding primary tumor disruption during excision is critical in oncological surgery.
back:
• Prevents local recurrence
• Minimizes iatrogenic seeding of malignant cells
• Essential for obtaining a definitive cure in localized disease

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Distinguish between 'Multidisciplinary' and 'Multiprofessional' teams as defined in modern cancer care.
back:
• Multidisciplinary: Includes various medical specialists (pathologists, surgeons, radiologists).
• Multiprofessional: Includes medical and non-medical staff (specialist nurses, social workers).

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Define the components of the TNM staging system used by the UICC and AJCC.
back:
• T: Extent/size of primary tumor
• N: Involvement of regional lymph nodes
• M: Presence of distant metastases

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: The phenomenon where improved diagnostic technology identifies occult metastases, causing an apparent but artefactual increase in survival for both localized and advanced stages, is the [___].
back:
● Stage shift (Will Rogers phenomenon).
● Prognosis for individual stages improves.
● Overall population prognosis remains unchanged.
● Caused by migration of patients between stage categories.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A 60-year-old patient with unresectable carcinoma of the pancreatic head presents with severe obstructive jaundice. The palliative surgical procedure indicated to relieve this symptom is [___].
back:
● Biliary bypass.
● Common examples: Cholecysto-jejunostomy or choledocho-jejunostomy.
● Purpose: Alleviate jaundice and improve quality of life without attempting cure.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Explain the role and mechanism of sentinel node biopsy in the management of melanoma and breast cancer.
back:
● Identifies the first node(s) receiving lymphatic drainage.
● Uses radiolabelled colloid or dye injection.
● Gamma camera pinpointing allows targeted excision.
● Accurately stages the disease while minimizing surgical morbidity.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A patient with known colorectal cancer is found to have isolated liver metastases. Contrast the surgical approach for resectable vs. multiple unresectable hepatic lesions.
back:
● Resectable: Radical surgical resection (offers ~33% long-term survival).
● Unresectable: In situ ablation techniques.
● Modalities: Cryotherapy or radiofrequency energy (RFA).
● Goal: Local control of metastatic spread.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Identify the core principle of radical surgery for solid tumours regarding the extent of tissue removal.
back:
● Excision of the primary tumour.
● Removal of a margin of surrounding healthy tissue.
● Clearance of regional lymph node drainage.
● Objective: Ensure local control and prevent lymphatic spread.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: In patients with malignant ascites where imaging is inconclusive, the surgical procedure [___] is the gold standard for obtaining tissue for diagnosis and staging.
back:
● Diagnostic Laparoscopy.
● Identifies small peritoneal/liver metastases missed on CT.
● Allows direct visualization and biopsy of suspicious lesions.
● Minimally invasive compared to laparotomy.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A 70-year-old male with an inoperable caecal tumour presents with vomiting and abdominal distension. Suggest a surgical intervention to manage his symptoms.
back:
● Palliative bypass procedure.
● Specifically: Ileo-transverse anastomosis.
● Goal: Alleviate symptoms of bowel obstruction.
● No effect on ultimate oncological outcome/survival.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Describe the clinical significance of meticulous surgical technique and 'non-disruption' during primary tumour excision.
back:
● Essential for obtaining a definitive cure in localized disease.
● Prevents accidental seeding of cancer cells.
● Crucial for reducing the risk of local recurrence.
● More vital than 'ultra-radical' margins in many cancers.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Contrast the definitions of 'multidisciplinary' versus 'multiprofessional' teams in cancer management.
back:
● Multidisciplinary: Various medically qualified specialists (e.g., surgeons, radiologists, pathologists).
● Multiprofessional: Includes non-medical specialists (e.g., specialist nurses, social workers, physiotherapists).
● Goal: Holistic, evidence-based patient management.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: List the primary surgical roles in the management of solid tumours besides curative resection.
back:
● Diagnosis (e.g., biopsy, orchidectomy).
● Staging (e.g., laparoscopy, sentinel node biopsy).
● Palliation (e.g., bypass, symptom relief).
● Prevention and Reconstruction.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: The paradox where improved imaging detects occult metastases, causing an apparent increase in survival rates for individual stages while overall survival remains unchanged, is known as the [___].
back:
Stage shift (or Will Rogers phenomenon).
- Caused by enriched prognosis in each stage group.
- Overall group prognosis remains static.
- Result of modern imaging technology advances.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A 65-year-old male with inoperable caecal cancer presents with vomiting and abdominal distension. To alleviate the obstruction, an ileo-transverse anastomosis is performed. This surgical role is classified as [___].
back:
Surgical Palliation.
- Alleviates symptoms (obstruction).
- Does not attempt to cure primary disease.
- Focuses on improving quality of life.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Explain the biological rationale behind radical surgery for localized solid tumors.
back:
Removal of primary tumor with wide margins.
- Excision of regional lymph node drainage.
- Prevents local recurrence.
- Inhibits early lymphatic spread of cancer cells.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Contrast the surgical approach for liver metastases in colorectal cancer with pulmonary metastases in renal cell carcinoma.
back:
Colorectal Liver Mets: Resection or in-situ ablation (RFA/cryotherapy); can lead to 1/3rd long-term survival.
- Renal Lung Mets: Pulmonary resection for isolated metastases.
- Both represent curative-intent surgery for metastatic disease.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Name the primary surgical objective when managing malignant ascites where cross-sectional imaging is inconclusive.
back:
Diagnosis and Staging.
- Laparoscopy is used to obtain tissue.
- Detects peritoneal disease or small liver metastases.
- Guides the decision between local vs systemic therapy.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: In the management of breast cancer, the procedure involving the injection of a radiolabelled colloid to identify the first draining lymph node for histological assessment is [___].
back:
Sentinel node biopsy.
- Pinpoints the node nearest the tumor.
- Uses a gamma camera for detection.
- Avoids unnecessary radical axillary dissection.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A patient with unresectable pancreatic head cancer presents with severe pruritus and jaundice. Surgeons perform a cholecysto-jejunostomy. What is the mechanism of symptomatic relief?
back:
Biliary Bypass.
- Diverts bile flow around the obstructing tumor.
- Alleviates jaundice and associated symptoms.
- Classic example of palliative surgical intervention.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Why is meticulous surgical technique emphasized during the excision of a primary tumor, even when radical margins are planned?
back:
Prevents tumor disruption/spillage.
- Avoids seeding cancer cells into the operative field.
- Minimizes the risk of local recurrence.
- Essential for achieving a surgical cure.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Distinguish between the composition of 'multidisciplinary' and 'multiprofessional' teams in cancer management.
back:
Multidisciplinary: Medically qualified specialists (surgeons, pathologists, radiologists).
- Multiprofessional: Includes non-medical specialists (nurses, social workers, physiotherapists).
- Both aim to ensure appropriate, individualized patient management.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: State the definitive treatment modality that offers the only realistic hope of cure for most solid tumors.
back:
Surgery.
- Remains the primary curative intervention.
- Role depends on localization vs widespread disease.
- Complemented by radiation or systemic therapies.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: In the surgical staging of breast cancer or melanoma, the lymph node nearest to the tumor identified using radiolabelled colloid is known as the [___].
back:
• Sentinel lymph node
• Pinpointed using a gamma camera
• Removed for histological diagnosis to determine if further nodal clearance is required.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A hospital reports increased survival rates for individual cancer stages after upgrading to high-resolution CT, but the total population survival remains unchanged. Identify this phenomenon.
back:
• Stage Shift (Will Rogers Phenomenon)
• Occurs when better imaging detects occult metastases
• Patients move from localized to metastatic groups, improving the statistical prognosis of both categories.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Explain the biological rationale and surgical components involved in 'radical surgery' for solid tumors.
back:
• Removal of the primary tumor with wide margins
• Excision of surrounding tissue and regional lymph node drainage
• Aim: To achieve local control and prevent lymphatic spread.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Contrast the surgical management goals for a patient with localized cecal cancer versus a patient with cecal cancer causing obstruction and unresectable liver metastases.
back:
• Localized: Curative radical resection (removal of tumor and nodes)
• Metastatic: Palliative bypass (e.g., ileo-transverse anastomosis)
• Shift from intent-to-cure to symptom relief and quality of life.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Differentiate between the 'multidisciplinary' and 'multiprofessional' components of a modern oncology team.
back:
• Multidisciplinary: Medically qualified specialists (surgeons, oncologists, pathologists, radiologists)
• Multiprofessional: Includes non-medical specialists (nurses, social workers, physiotherapists, speech therapists)
• Goal: Ensure comprehensive, patient-centered care plans.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: The global standard for classifying the extent of cancer based on the primary tumor size, regional node involvement, and distant spread is the [___] system.
back:
• TNM (Tumour, Nodes, Metastases) system
• Maintained by UICC and AJCC
• Essential for determining if treatment should be locoregional or systemic.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A patient with colorectal cancer is found to have isolated liver metastases. Name two surgical techniques used to manage these metastases for potential long-term survival.
back:
• Surgical resection (metastasectomy)
• In situ ablation (using radiofrequency energy or cryotherapy)
• Success provides the only realistic hope of long-term survival in metastatic colorectal disease.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Describe the specific surgical mechanism used to palliate obstructive jaundice in a patient with an unresectable tumor at the head of the pancreas.
back:
• Biliary bypass procedure
• Cholecysto-jejunostomy or choledocho-jejunostomy
• Objective: Divert bile flow into the jejunum to alleviate jaundice and pruritus.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Contrast the utility of cross-sectional imaging (CT/MRI) with laparoscopy in the staging of gastric or esophageal cancer.
back:
• Imaging: Evaluates gross primary size and bulky distant metastases
• Laparoscopy: Detects small peritoneal seedlings and liver surface nodules missed by scans
• Laparoscopic ultrasound: Adjunct for identifying deep intrahepatic metastases.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Identify three clinical examples where the primary role of the surgical procedure is diagnosis rather than tumor removal.
back:
• Laparoscopy for malignant ascites (tissue biopsy)
• Lymph node biopsy for suspected lymphoma
• Orchidectomy for suspected testicular cancer
• Sentinel node biopsy in breast cancer/melanoma.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: The paradox where improved imaging techniques detect occult metastases, leading to an apparent 'improvement' in stage-specific survival without changing overall population prognosis, is known as [___].
back:
- Will Rogers phenomenon (Stage Shift).
- Results from shifting patients with poor prognosis into a more advanced stage category.
- No change in pooled survival for the entire group.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A 65-year-old male with unresectable head of pancreas carcinoma presents with severe obstructive jaundice. The palliative surgical procedure indicated to relieve this symptom is [___].
back:
- Cholecysto-jejunostomy or choledocho-jejunostomy.
- Aim: Bypass the biliary obstruction.
- Purpose: Improve quality of life (palliation) without curative intent.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Explain the biological rationale and components of 'radical surgery' for solid tumours.
back:
- Removal of the primary tumour.
- Excision of a margin of surrounding healthy tissue.
- Removal of regional lymph node drainage to prevent lymphatic spread.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Contrast the surgical approach for resectable liver metastases in colorectal cancer versus multiple, unresectable liver lesions.
back:
- Resectable: Meticulous surgical resection (leads to ~33% long-term survival).
- Unresectable: In situ ablation using cryotherapy or radiofrequency energy.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Identify two specific malignancies where 'Sentinel Node Biopsy' is the preferred surgical staging technique for regional lymph nodes.
back:
- Malignant Melanoma.
- Breast Cancer.
- Uses radiolabelled colloid/dye to identify the node nearest the tumour.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: In patients with suspected intra-abdominal malignancy and malignant ascites, the gold-standard surgical procedure for obtaining tissue and staging is [___].
back:
- Laparoscopy.
- Useful for detecting peritoneal disease and small liver metastases missed on CT/MRI.
- Often uses laparoscopic ultrasound as an adjunct.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A patient presents with an inoperable caecal cancer causing progressive bowel obstruction. Name the palliative surgical procedure used to alleviate the obstructive symptoms.
back:
- Ileo-transverse anastomosis.
- It bypasses the obstructed segment to restore bowel continuity.
- Focus is on symptomatic relief rather than survival extension.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Differentiate between 'Multidisciplinary' and 'Multiprofessional' teams according to standard oncological principles.
back:
- Multidisciplinary: Various medically qualified specialists (e.g., Surgeon, Pathologist, Radiologist).
- Multiprofessional: Includes non-medical specialists (e.g., Nurses, Social workers, Physiotherapists).

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Contrast the role of surgery in primary tumour management versus isolated pulmonary metastatic disease from Renal Cell Carcinoma (RCC).
back:
- Primary: Radical nephrectomy for local control and cure.
- Metastatic: Pulmonary resection (metastasectomy) for isolated lung lesions to improve long-term survival.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: What is the primary technical goal during the excision of a primary tumour to prevent local recurrence?
back:
- Meticulous surgery to ensure the tumour is not disrupted or 'spilled' during excision.
- Ensures clear histological margins.
- Essential for obtaining a cure in localized disease.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Radical surgery for cancer involves removal of the primary tumor along with surrounding tissue and its associated [___] to ensure local control.
back:
* Lymph node drainage
* Prevents spread through lymphatics
* Aims for definitive local cure

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A 55-year-old male with colorectal cancer presents with two isolated lesions in the right lobe of the liver. The primary surgical objective for these lesions is [___].
back:
* Removal of metastatic disease
* Can achieve long-term survival in ~33% of patients
* May involve resection or in-situ ablation (e.g., cryotherapy)

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Describe the procedural mechanism of sentinel node biopsy in the staging of breast cancer or melanoma.
back:
* Radiolabelled colloid is injected around the tumor
* Gamma camera identifies the first draining node
* Node is removed for histological diagnosis

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Contrast the clinical purpose of an ileo-transverse anastomosis in inoperable caecal cancer versus a radical right hemicolectomy.
back:
* Ileo-transverse: Palliative (relieves obstruction symptoms)
* Radical Hemicolectomy: Curative (removes primary tumor and nodes)
* Intent: Symptom relief vs. disease eradication

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
coreConcept: Role of Laparoscopy in Cancer Staging
front: Explain why laparoscopy is frequently used for staging intra-abdominal malignancies like gastric or oesophageal cancer despite modern cross-sectional imaging.
back:
* Detects small liver metastases missed by scans
* Identifies widespread peritoneal disease
* Provides tissue for histological confirmation

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: The phenomenon where improved staging technology causes an apparent improvement in stage-specific prognosis without changing overall survival is known as [___].
back:
* Stage shift (Will Rogers phenomenon)
* Artefactual improvement in survival stats
* Occurs due to detection of occult metastases

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A patient with unresectable carcinoma of the head of the pancreas presents with severe jaundice and pruritus. Name the appropriate surgical intervention for symptom relief.
back:
* Surgical bypass (Palliative surgery)
* Cholecysto-jejunostomy or Choledocho-jejunostomy
* Relieves biliary obstruction to improve quality of life

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Identify the primary advantage of the multidisciplinary team (MDT) approach in managing complex cancers.
back:
* Simultaneous expert opinions from multiple specialties
* Transparent and explicit decision-making
* Ensures patient receives the most appropriate care plan

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Contrast the use of in-situ ablation with cryotherapy versus traditional surgical resection for liver metastases.
back:
* Ablation: Uses radiofrequency/cold energy to destroy tissue in-place
* Resection: Physical removal of the metastatic segment
* Both: Aim to eliminate detectable metastatic disease

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: List three distinct roles of surgery in cancer management other than primary tumor removal.
back:
* Diagnosis and Staging (e.g., Biopsy)
* Palliation (e.g., Bypass)
* Reconstruction and Prevention

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: In sentinel node biopsy for melanoma or breast cancer, a radiolabelled colloid is injected to identify the node nearest the tumor using a [___].
back: Gamma camera. This procedure pinpoints the first draining lymph node for histological diagnosis to assess early lymphatic spread.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A 70-year-old male with inoperable caecal cancer presents with worsening abdominal distention and vomiting. Identify the most appropriate surgical palliative procedure.
back: Ileo-transverse anastomosis. This bypass procedure alleviates symptoms of bowel obstruction without attempting to cure the primary malignancy.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Explain why meticulous surgical technique during primary tumor excision is vital even if radical surgery does not always prevent systemic metastasis.
back:
- Ensures local control of the disease.
- Prevents local recurrence.
- Avoids accidental disruption or seeding of the primary tumor during excision.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Contrast the composition of a 'multidisciplinary' team with a 'multiprofessional' team in the context of oncology management.
back:
- Multidisciplinary: Various medically qualified specialists like surgeons, pathologists, and radiologists.
- Multiprofessional: Includes non-medical specialists like nurses, social workers, and physiotherapists.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Describe the 'Will Rogers phenomenon' (stage shift) occurring due to advances in diagnostic imaging technology.
back:
- Improved imaging detects occult metastases earlier.
- Patients shift from 'localised' to 'metastatic' stages.
- This causes an artefactual improvement in survival rates per stage while overall prognosis remains unchanged.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Successful resection of liver metastases arising specifically from [___] cancer can lead to long-term survival in approximately one-third of patients.
back: Colorectal cancer. In cases with multiple metastases, in-situ ablation using radiofrequency energy or cryotherapy may be utilized.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A patient with suspected intra-abdominal malignancy presents with malignant ascites. Identify the surgical intervention used to obtain tissue for diagnosis and staging when imaging is inconclusive.
back: Laparoscopy. It allows direct visualization and biopsy of peritoneal disease or small liver metastases that may be missed on CT/MRI.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Evaluate the clinical utility of pulmonary resection in the management of metastatic renal cell carcinoma.
back:
- Used for isolated lung metastases.
- Can be curative in selected patients.
- Follows the principle of removing metastatic disease when the primary is controlled.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Distinguish between the curative and palliative goals of surgery in a patient presenting with an unresectable carcinoma of the pancreatic head.
back:
- Curative: Radical resection (e.g., Whipple's) to remove all tumor tissue.
- Palliative: Bypass procedures (e.g., choledocho-jejunostomy) to alleviate jaundice or gastric outlet obstruction.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: List the five major roles surgery plays in comprehensive cancer management besides the removal of the primary tumor.
back:
- Diagnosis and Staging.
- Removal of metastatic disease.
- Palliation of symptoms.
- Prevention of cancer.
- Reconstruction and rehabilitation.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: The phenomenon where improved diagnostic technology identifies occult metastases, causing patients to move from a 'localized' stage to an 'advanced' stage and artificially improving survival statistics for both, is called the [___].
back:
* **Will Rogers Phenomenon (Stage Shift)**.
* Artificial improvement in stage-specific prognosis.
* No change in the overall group survival rate.
* Driven by more sensitive imaging (e.g., modern CT vs. 1980s X-ray).

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A 65-year-old male with unresectable carcinoma of the head of the pancreas presents with severe obstructive jaundice. Name the palliative surgical procedure indicated to relieve this symptom.
back:
* **Cholecysto-jejunostomy or Choledocho-jejunostomy**.
* Role: Palliative bypass.
* Objective: Relieve biliary obstruction and jaundice.
* Goal: Improve quality of life without expecting a cure.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Explain the biological rationale and method for identifying the 'sentinel node' in breast cancer management.
back:
* **Rationale**: The first node receiving drainage from the tumor is the most likely to harbor metastases.
* **Method**: Injecting radiolabelled colloid or dye around the tumor.
* **Significance**: If negative, avoids unnecessary radical axillary dissection.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A patient with colon cancer has 1-3 regional lymph node involvements but no distant metastases. Contrast the TNM classification with the Dukes staging for this specific scenario.
back:
* **TNM**: N1, M0 (Stage III).
* **Dukes**: Dukes C.
* **Significance**: Lymph node involvement automatically classifies the disease as Stage III/Dukes C regardless of primary tumor depth (T).

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Identify the surgical approach used to obtain tissue for diagnosis and staging in a patient with suspected malignant ascites where imaging is inconclusive.
back:
* **Laparoscopy**.
* Enables direct visualization of peritoneal surfaces.
* Allows biopsy of small liver metastases missed by CT.
* Essential for staging gastric and esophageal cancers.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: The primary goal of [___] surgery is the removal of the primary tumor with an adequate margin of normal tissue and regional lymph nodes to ensure local control.
back:
* **Radical Surgery**.
* Focuses on en-bloc resection.
* Includes primary tumor and lymphatic drainage.
* Aimed at preventing local recurrence and achieving cure.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A patient with colorectal cancer is found to have isolated liver metastases. Discuss the role and success rate of surgical intervention in this stage IV scenario.
back:
* **Role**: Resection of metastatic disease (Metastasectomy).
* **Method**: Surgical excision or in-situ ablation (Cryotherapy/RFA).
* **Outcome**: Successful resection leads to long-term survival in approximately one-third of patients.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Differentiate between a 'multidisciplinary' and a 'multiprofessional' team within a surgical oncology unit.
back:
* **Multidisciplinary**: Includes various medically qualified specialists (e.g., Surgeon, Oncologist, Radiologist).
* **Multiprofessional**: Includes specialists from non-medical backgrounds (e.g., Nurses, Social workers, Physiotherapists).

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Contrast the intent and clinical outcomes of an ileo-transverse anastomosis in inoperable cecal cancer versus a radical right hemicolectomy.
back:
* **Ileo-transverse anastomosis**: Palliative bypass; relieves obstruction symptoms; does not remove tumor or extend life significantly.
* **Radical right hemicolectomy**: Curative intent; removes primary tumor and nodes; aimed at long-term survival.
