category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Define the 'Will Rogers Phenomenon' (stage shift) as it relates to modern cancer imaging technology.
back:
Improved imaging detects occult metastases earlier.
- Patients shift from 'localised' to 'metastatic' stages.
- Artificially improves survival statistics for all stages without changing overall population survival.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: For patients presenting with malignant ascites where cross-sectional imaging is inconclusive, the surgical procedure of choice to obtain tissue for diagnosis is [___].
back:
Laparoscopy.
- Essential for obtaining tissue biopsy.
- Identifies peritoneal disease or small liver metastases missed on CT/MRI.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A patient with gastric cancer undergoes staging laparoscopy. Identify two findings that would classify the disease as non-curative/inoperable during this procedure.
back:
Widespread peritoneal disease.
- Small intrahepatic metastases.
- Laparoscopic ultrasound is a useful adjunct for intrahepatic detection.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Contrast the composition and purpose of a Multidisciplinary Team (MDT) versus a Multiprofessional Team in oncology.
back:
MDT: Includes various medically qualified specialists (surgeons, pathologists, radiologists).
- Multiprofessional: Includes non-medical specialists (nurses, social workers, physiotherapists) for holistic rehabilitation and care.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Contrast the outcomes of 'Radical surgery' versus 'Ultra-radical surgery' regarding the development of metastatic disease in breast cancer.
back:
Radical surgery provides local control.
- Ultra-radical surgery (excessive margins) has little to no effect on preventing the development of distant metastatic disease compared to radical/simple procedures.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
coreConcept: In situ ablation techniques for metastases
front: Name two non-surgical energy-based methods used for in situ ablation of multiple liver metastases when anatomical resection is not feasible.
back:
Cryotherapy.
- Radiofrequency energy (RFA).
- These allow for local control of disease in the place (in situ).

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: In the TNM staging system used for clinical oncology, the 'N' category specifically assesses the extent and involvement of [___].
back:
- Regional lymph nodes.
- Assesses presence, number, and location of nodal metastases.
- Critical for determining locoregional versus systemic treatment.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A hospital adopts PET-CT imaging for staging lung cancer. While individual stage survival rates appear to 'improve,' the overall survival for all patients remains static. Identify this phenomenon.
back:
- Stage Shift or Will Rogers Phenomenon.
- Occurs when sensitive imaging detects occult metastases.
- Patients move from localized to advanced stages, improving the statistical prognosis of both groups without changing overall outcome.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Explain the biological mechanism used to identify the 'sentinel lymph node' during surgical staging for breast cancer or melanoma.
back:
- Radiolabelled colloid or dye is injected around the primary tumor.
- Substance drains to the first-echelon node (sentinel node).
- Identified via gamma camera or visualization to assess for early lymphatic spread.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Contrast the surgical management goals for a localized T2N0 rectal cancer versus an advanced gastric cancer with malignant ascites and peritoneal seedlings.
back:
- Localized T2N0: Curative intent via radical resection of tumor and lymphatics.
- Advanced with Ascites: Palliative intent; surgery limited to diagnosis (laparoscopy) or symptom relief (bypass) rather than cure.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: State the three primary components involved in performing 'radical surgery' for a solid epithelial malignancy.
back:
- Excision of the primary tumor.
- Removal of a margin of surrounding healthy tissue.
- Clearance of the regional lymph node drainage basin.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: In the staging of intra-abdominal malignancies like oesophageal or gastric cancer, [___] is the gold-standard surgical procedure to detect small liver metastases or peritoneal disease missed by CT.
back:
- Diagnostic Laparoscopy.
- Often combined with laparoscopic ultrasound.
- Prevents unnecessary laparotomies in patients with occult widespread disease.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A 60-year-old patient presents with a history of colorectal cancer and two isolated, resectable lesions in the right hepatic lobe. Determine the appropriate surgical role here.
back:
- Resection of metastatic disease.
- Curative intent (not palliative).
- Successful resection of liver metastases from colorectal cancer leads to long-term survival in ~33% of patients.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Differentiate the modern diagnostic approach for Hodgkin's Lymphoma from the historical surgical standard used in the mid-20th century.
back:
- Historical: Routine staging laparotomy and splenectomy.
- Modern: Redundant due to high-resolution cross-sectional imaging (CT/PET) and the efficacy of systemic chemotherapy.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Distinguish between 'multidisciplinary' and 'multiprofessional' teams in the context of a hospital oncology board.
back:
- Multidisciplinary: Includes various medically qualified specialists (e.g., surgeons, radiologists, pathologists).
- Multiprofessional: Includes specialists from non-medical backgrounds (e.g., specialist nurses, social workers, physiotherapists).

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Identify the specific palliative surgical procedure used to relieve obstructive jaundice in a patient with unresectable carcinoma of the pancreatic head.
back:
- Biliary bypass procedure.
- Specifically: Cholecysto-jejunostomy or choledocho-jejunostomy.
- Relieves symptoms and improves quality of life without removing the primary cancer.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: In patients with intra-abdominal malignancies, [___] is a particularly useful surgical adjunct for the specific diagnosis of intrahepatic metastases.
back: Laparoscopic ultrasound.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A 25-year-old male presents with a painless, firm testicular lump. Unlike most other solid tumours where a needle biopsy is preferred, the primary surgical procedure required for both diagnosis and initial treatment is [___].
back: Radical orchidectomy.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Explain the biological principle of 'selective toxicity' as it applies to determining the optimal dose in non-surgical cancer treatments.
back: • Maximize toxicity to the tumour. • Spare normal tissues from damage. • Achieve the maximal probability of an uncomplicated cure.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A surgeon considers an ultra-radical mastectomy to prevent distant spread. Based on randomized trials, contrast the impact of this approach versus simple mastectomy regarding distant metastases and survival.
back: • Local control: Improved with radical surgery. • Distant metastases: No significant difference. • Survival: Comparable between both techniques.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Besides diagnosis, staging, and removal of disease, identify two other essential roles of surgery in comprehensive cancer management.
back: • Prevention (prophylaxis). • Reconstruction (restoration of form/function).

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Pulmonary resection for isolated lung metastases is a recognized surgical intervention, particularly for patients with [___] carcinoma.
back: Renal cell carcinoma.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A patient's pharmacogenomic profile indicates 'Normal sensitivity' in healthy tissues but 'Increased sensitivity' in the tumour. According to precision medicine principles, how should the dose be adjusted?
back: Use a lower dose to achieve cure while minimizing toxicity.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Describe the clinical implication of the 'sigmoidal' shape of the dose-response curve for both cancer cure and tissue damage.
back: Over a narrow dose range, outcomes shift rapidly from failure to success (cure) or from tolerability to severe tissue damage.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Contrast the pathological criteria for T3a versus T3d staging in the TNM system for colorectal cancer.
back: • T3a: Minimal invasion (<1 mm beyond muscularis propria). • T3d: Extensive invasion (>15 mm beyond muscularis propria).

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Mention the two primary reasons why staging laparotomy, once central to lymphoma management, is now considered largely redundant.
back: • Improved accuracy of cross-sectional imaging (CT/PET). • Increased efficacy of systemic chemotherapy.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: The surgical adjunct [___] is specifically utilized during staging to detect small intrahepatic metastases that standard cross-sectional imaging often misses.
back: • Laparoscopic ultrasound. • It provides high-resolution imaging of the liver parenchyma directly.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A patient's tumor is found to be resistant (R) to a specific treatment, but their normal tissues show normal sensitivity (N). Based on precision medicine principles, the recommended dose adjustment is to [___].
back: • Use a higher dose. • This attempts to overcome tumor resistance when normal tissue tolerance allows for it.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Explain the principle of 'Selective Toxicity' as it applies to non-surgical cancer management.
back: • Treatment should be selectively toxic to the tumor cells. • It must spare normal tissues from permanent or severe damage as much as possible.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Contrast the quantification methods used for surgical oncology versus non-surgical modalities like radiotherapy.
back: • Surgery: Difficult to quantify; no standard measurement units. • Radiotherapy/Drugs: Expressed in reproducible units (e.g., Grays for radiation, milligrams for drugs).

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Describe the characteristic shape and clinical implication of the dose-response curve for non-surgical cancer therapies.
back: • Shape: Sigmoidal (S-shaped). • Implication: Small dose changes can lead to a rapid transition from treatment failure to success, or from safety to severe toxicity.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: The application of molecular biology and pharmacogenomics to tailor cancer treatment to an individual's specific tumor sensitivity is termed [___].
back: • Precision Medicine (or Personalised Medicine). • It aims to maximize the probability of an uncomplicated cure.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A 22-year-old male presents with a suspicious, firm testicular mass. The surgical procedure required to simultaneously provide tissue for diagnosis and primary treatment is [___].
back: • Diagnostic Orchidectomy. • Surgery is central here because biopsy risks scrotal seeding or inaccurate staging.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Explain how the 'optimal dose' for a specific cancer treatment is determined using dose-response curves.
back: • It is the dose that provides the maximal probability of an uncomplicated cure. • It represents the best balance between tumor cure rate and normal tissue damage.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Contrast the surgical roles of 'Prevention' and 'Reconstruction' in a patient with a high genetic risk for malignancy.
back: • Prevention: Removing high-risk tissues before cancer develops (e.g., prophylactic mastectomy). • Reconstruction: Restoring form/function after cancer surgery (e.g., breast implants).

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Identify the standard SI unit used to measure the absorbed dose of ionizing radiation in clinical oncology.
back: • The Gray (Gy). • One Gray equals the absorption of one joule of energy per kilogram of tissue.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: In the TNM staging of colorectal cancer, the specific T-stage used to describe a tumour that has perforated the visceral peritoneum is [___].
back: T4b. This indicates the tumour has extended through the bowel wall and breached the visceral peritoneal surface, representing a high risk for peritoneal seeding.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A 24-year-old male presents with a hard, painless testicular mass. Explain why a radical orchidectomy is performed rather than a simple percutaneous needle biopsy for diagnosis.
back: Percutaneous biopsy is contraindicated because it risks breaching the tunica albuginea and causing lymphatic seeding to the inguinal nodes. Orchidectomy provides both the histological diagnosis and the primary surgical treatment.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Explain the fundamental difference between surgery and non-surgical therapies (radiotherapy/chemotherapy) regarding the quantification of treatment 'dose'.
back: Non-surgical therapies are quantified in reproducible units (Grays or milligrams) allowing for dose-response curves. Surgery lacks standard units; its efficacy is qualitative and operator-dependent, making sigmoidal dose-response modeling impossible.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A pathology report for a colon resection describes a tumor invading the submucosa but not reaching the muscularis propria. Contrast this finding with a T2-staged tumor.
back: The described tumor is T1 (invasion of submucosa). A T2 tumor is more advanced, requiring invasion into the muscularis propria. Both are categorized as Dukes A if nodes are negative.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: In the context of 'Personalised Medicine', determine the appropriate dose adjustment if a patient's normal tissues and tumour both exhibit increased sensitivity (S) to a drug.
back: The dose should be lowered. This adjustment exploits the tumour's increased sensitivity for cure while preventing excessive, permanent damage to the equally sensitive normal tissues.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: During laparoscopic staging for intra-abdominal malignancies, the specific adjunct used to detect small, occult liver metastases missed by CT imaging is [___].
back: Laparoscopic Ultrasound. It provides high-resolution imaging directly on the liver surface, identifying lesions too small or iso-attenuating for standard cross-sectional imaging.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A patient with Hodgkin’s Lymphoma requires staging. Explain why the historical practice of 'Staging Laparotomy' has been largely abandoned in modern oncology.
back: The procedure is redundant due to highly accurate non-invasive imaging (PET/CT) and the widespread use of systemic chemotherapy, which treats occult abdominal disease without requiring surgical confirmation.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A patient receives a chemotherapy dose that results in severe permanent organ damage rather than a cure. Explain this outcome using the sigmoidal dose-response curve mechanism.
back: The dose exceeded the 'optimal dose' range. In sigmoidal curves, a narrow dose increase can shift the outcome from a 'probability of uncomplicated cure' to the 'toxicity range' for normal tissues.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Contrast a 'Multidisciplinary' team from a 'Multiprofessional' team based on the professional backgrounds of their members.
back: Multidisciplinary teams consist of various medically qualified specialists (e.g., Surgeons, Radiologists). Multiprofessional teams include specialists from non-medical backgrounds (e.g., Social workers, Macmillan nurses, Physiotherapists).

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Apart from diagnosis, staging, and curative/palliative resection, identify the two additional surgical roles in cancer management focused on prevention and restoration.
back:
1. Prophylactic (Preventative) surgery (e.g., removing pre-malignant polyps).
2. Reconstructive surgery (e.g., breast reconstruction post-mastectomy to restore form and function).

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: In the management of melanoma and breast cancer, the technique of identifying the first draining lymph node using radiolabelled colloid is known as [___] biopsy.
back:
Sentinel node biopsy.

*   Identifies node nearest to tumor.
*   Gamma camera pinpointing.
*   Used for histological staging.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A patient with unresectable carcinoma of the head of the pancreas presents with severe obstructive jaundice. Name the palliative surgical bypass indicated.
back:
Cholecysto-jejunostomy or Choledocho-jejunostomy.

*   Alleviates biliary obstruction.
*   Improves quality of life.
*   Does not affect overall survival.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Explain the anatomical objective of radical surgery for a primary solid tumor.
back:
Excision of the primary tumor plus surrounding tissue and regional lymph node drainage.

*   Ensures local control.
*   Prevents lymphatic spread.
*   Meticulous technique prevents tumor seeding.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Contrast radical surgery with ultra-radical surgery outcomes in breast cancer based on randomized trials.
back: Radical surgery provides local control; ultra-radical surgery shows no additional benefit in preventing metastatic disease or improving survival compared to simple radical excision.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Describe the clinical significance of the 'Will Rogers phenomenon' (stage shift) in oncology.
back:
Better imaging detects occult metastases, shifting patients to higher stages.

*   Artificial improvement in stage-specific prognosis.
*   Overall survival remains unchanged.
*   Due to stage enrichment.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: For patients presenting with malignant ascites of unknown origin, the preferred surgical diagnostic procedure to obtain tissue is [___].
back:
Laparoscopy.

*   Direct visualization of peritoneum.
*   Identifies small liver metastases.
*   Used when imaging is inconclusive.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A patient with a history of colorectal cancer presents with a solitary liver metastasis. What is the surgical management and prognosis?
back:
Surgical resection of the metastasis.

*   Potential for long-term survival in 33% of patients.
*   Ablation (cryotherapy/radiofrequency) is an alternative.
*   Indicated if disease is localized.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Explain how meticulous surgical handling of the tumor influences the risk of local recurrence.
back: Preventing tumor disruption during excision avoids accidental 'seeding' of malignant cells into the surgical field, which is essential for achieving a definitive local cure.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Distinguish between 'multidisciplinary' and 'multiprofessional' teams in cancer management.
back: Multidisciplinary includes various medical specialists (surgeons, pathologists, radiologists). Multiprofessional includes non-medical staff (nurses, social workers, physiotherapists).

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Suggest a palliative surgical bypass for a patient with an inoperable caecal cancer causing bowel obstruction.
back:
Ileo-transverse anastomosis.

*   Bypasses the site of obstruction.
*   Relieves obstructive symptoms.
*   Improves quality of life in late-stage disease.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: The paradox where improved diagnostic technology leads to higher cure rates in every stage without changing overall survival is known as the [___].
back:
● Will Rogers phenomenon (Stage shift)
● Occurs when occult metastases are detected earlier
● Redistributes patients to more advanced stages
● Enriches prognosis of both early and late-stage groups artefactually.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A patient with inoperable cecal cancer presents with bowel obstruction. Name the most appropriate palliative surgical intervention to alleviate symptoms.
back:
● Ileo-transverse anastomosis
● Goal: Symptom relief (bypass of obstruction)
● Objective: Improved quality of life rather than cure
● Outcome: No effect on ultimate disease survival.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Explain the role of radical surgery in the management of solid tumors.
back:
● Removal of primary tumor
● Excision of surrounding tissue and lymph node drainage
● Objective: Ensure local control
● Objective: Prevent lymphatic spread.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A 55-year-old male with known colorectal cancer is found to have multiple liver metastases on CT. Under what specific surgical condition is a 'cure' still potentially achievable?
back:
● Successful resection of all detectable disease
● Long-term survival occurs in roughly one-third of these patients
● Alternative: In situ ablation (Cryotherapy or Radiofrequency energy).

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Identify the primary surgical procedure used for both diagnosis and staging in patients with suspected gastric cancer and malignant ascites.
back:
● Laparoscopy
● Identifies widespread peritoneal disease
● Detects small liver metastases missed by cross-sectional imaging
● Often combined with laparoscopic ultrasound.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: In patients with melanoma or breast cancer, the diagnostic technique used to pinpoint and remove the lymph node nearest to the tumor is [___].
back:
● Sentinel node biopsy
● Involves injection of radiolabelled colloid
● Uses a gamma camera for localization
● Provides histological confirmation of nodal status.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A patient presents with a symptomatic primary tumor and confirmed distant metastases. What is the surgical priority in this scenario?
back:
● Surgical Palliation
● Objective: Relieve symptoms (e.g., bypass jaundice or obstruction)
● Outcome: Increased quality of life
● Note: Does not change the patient's ultimate prognosis.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Contrast the composition of 'multidisciplinary' teams versus 'multiprofessional' teams in an oncology setting.
back:
● Multidisciplinary: Medically qualified specialists (surgeons, pathologists, radiologists)
● Multiprofessional: Includes non-medical specialists (nurses, social workers, speech therapists)
● Goal: Integrated patient management and shared decision-making.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Distinguish the surgical role of 'reconstruction' from 'palliation' in cancer management.
back:
● Reconstruction: Restoring form or function after radical primary excision
● Palliation: Alleviating distressing symptoms in incurable disease
● Examples: Plastic surgery flap (reconstruction) vs. Bypassing obstruction (palliation).

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: List three definitive surgical procedures used primarily for cancer diagnosis rather than treatment.
back:
● Orchidectomy (for suspected testicular cancer)
● Lymph node biopsy (for suspected lymphoma)
● Laparoscopic tissue biopsy (for malignant ascites).

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: In melanoma and breast cancer, the specific lymph node nearest to the primary tumor identified via radiolabeled colloid is called the [___].
back: Sentinel lymph node. • Pinpointed using a gamma camera. • Biopsied to determine histological staging and potential metastatic spread.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A hospital introduces high-resolution PET-CT, leading to improved survival rates for both Stage I and Stage IV cancer patients individually, but the overall population survival remains unchanged. This paradox is known as [___].
back: Will Rogers Phenomenon (Stage Shift). • Caused by migration of patients from lower to higher stages due to better detection. • Prognosis improves per stage but overall cure rate is static.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Explain the difference between a 'multidisciplinary' and a 'multiprofessional' team in the context of oncological management.
back: Multidisciplinary: Includes various medically qualified specialists (e.g., pathologists, surgeons, radiologists). • Multiprofessional: Includes specialists from non-medical backgrounds (e.g., nurses, social workers, physiotherapists).

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A surgeon performs a radical mastectomy instead of an ultra-radical procedure for breast cancer. Based on randomized trials, contrast the outcomes of these two approaches regarding local control and metastatic development.
back: Local Control: Both effective if primary tumor is not disrupted. • Metastatic Disease: Ultra-radical surgery does NOT significantly reduce risk of distant metastasis compared to radical surgery.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Identify the primary role of diagnostic laparoscopy in a patient presenting with malignant ascites and suspected intra-abdominal malignancy.
back: Obtaining tissue for histological diagnosis. • Detecting widespread peritoneal disease or small liver metastases missed on imaging. • Crucial for staging gastric and esophageal cancers.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: In the UICC/AJCC staging system, the 'N' category specifically represents the status of [___].
back: Regional lymph nodes. • NX: Cannot be assessed. • N0: No node metastasis. • N1/N2: Increasing degrees of regional node involvement.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: A patient with inoperable cecal cancer presents with symptoms of bowel obstruction. Describe the surgical procedure indicated for palliation in this case.
back: Ileo-transverse anastomosis. • Provides a bypass to alleviate obstruction symptoms. • Focuses on quality of life rather than curing the primary disease.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Under what specific clinical circumstances is surgical resection of liver metastases considered appropriate and potentially curative?
back: Metastases arising from colorectal cancer. • Requires successful resection of all detectable disease. • Can lead to long-term survival in approximately one-third of patients.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Contrast the primary objectives of curative cancer surgery versus palliative cancer surgery.
back: Curative: Complete removal of tumor, surrounding tissue, and lymph nodes for long-term survival. • Palliative: Symptom relief (e.g., bypassing jaundice) and improved quality of life without intent to cure.

category: Describe the basic principles and role of surgery in cancer management, including its use for curative and palliative purposes
front: Specify the initial surgical procedure required for both the diagnosis and management of a patient suspected of having testicular cancer.
back: Orchidectomy. • Provides tissue for definitive histological diagnosis. • Serves as the primary therapeutic removal of the tumor.
